why: I compared the builder brief with each verifier check. Most of the builder brief stays on the bar: it repeats the expect lines, tells the builder to run `npm test`, and asks it to write its own tests. Step 2 breaks the criterion. It says "Do not touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all (git diff on it must be empty)". That is the verifier's Check 4 probe, `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`, and its PASS condition, "no diff to it". No expect line or issue proof names that git diff command, so the builder is being handed the checker's method. Step 4 also mirrors the shape of the Check 3 fixture: "put a bad file after the missing one too", which matches the verifier's run of b.jsonl missing.jsonl c.jsonl where c is bad. Step 3 also repeats verifier advisories: "2 takes priority over 1" and print nothing on stdout for two `-` arguments. Advisories are not PASS/FAIL checks, though, so they don't break the criterion on their own. Because a verifier check leaks through, the criterion is not met.
